sentence: Freeport-McMoRan's revenue rose by 60.6% in fiscal 2021 [7].
The revenue for fiscal 2021 was $22,845 billion [7].
The revenue for the previous fiscal year (2020) was missing, but the growth percentage was calculated as 60.6% [7].
Sales volumes increased by 19% for copper and 59% for gold [3].
Realized prices increased by 47% for copper, 2% for gold, and 53% for molybdenum [7].
These factors contributed to the significant rise in revenue [3][7].
T-Mobile's revenue rose by 17.1% in fiscal 2021 [1][3].
Postpaid revenues increased by $6.3 billion, or 17%, primarily from higher average postpaid accounts and higher postpaid ARPA [3].
Prepaid revenues increased by $312 million, or 3%, due to higher prepaid ARPU and average prepaid customers [3].
Wholesale revenues increased by $1.2 billion, or 45%, mainly due to the Master Network Service Agreement with DISH and the success of other MVNO relationships [3].

Other service revenues increased by $245 million, or 12%, mainly from higher Lifeline revenues and inclusion of wireline operations from the Merger, partially offset by lower advertising revenues [2].

Equipment revenues increased by $3.4 billion, or 20%, mainly from an increase in the number of devices sold due to a larger customer base from the Merger, switching activity returning to more normalized levels, a higher upgrade rate, and the planned shift in device financing from leasing to EIP [3].
Booking Holdings' revenue rose by 61.2% in fiscal 2021 [6].
The revenue growth was driven by the significant improvement in travel demand trends since the second quarter of 2020, which was severely impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic [6][4][5].

Specifically, agency and merchant gross bookings increased, with merchant gross bookings growing more than agency gross bookings due to the expansion of merchant accommodation reservation services at Booking.com [5][6].
Additionally, the increase in room nights, accommodation ADRs, and the positive impact of foreign exchange rate fluctuations contributed to the growth in gross bookings [5][6].

The growth in revenues from online travel reservation services, including both agency and merchant revenues, was also due to the significant improvement in travel demand trends since the second quarter of 2020 [6].
Advertising and other revenues increased due to the recovery in travel and restaurant demand trends, as well as fees from restaurants using OpenTable's online reservation service [6].

The increase in revenue was also influenced by the timing of bookings versus travel, with a shorter booking window in 2021 leading to a lower percentage of revenue recognized compared to gross bookings [2][7].
Monster Beverage's revenue rose by 20.5% in fiscal 2021 [1][4].
This growth in revenue was primarily driven by an increase in net sales, which rose by 20.5% from $4,598,638 million in fiscal 2020 to $5,541,352 million in fiscal 2021 [4].
The company attributed this increase to the launching and/or relaunching of products and new products into new domestic and international markets and channels [4][5].
Phillips 66's revenue rose by 74% in fiscal 2021 [1][7].
The revenue growth was driven by higher prices for refined petroleum products, crude oil, and NGL, as well as increased volumes for refined petroleum products and crude oil [7][2].
Additionally, there was an increase in equity in earnings of affiliates, mainly due to higher equity earnings from CPChem, WRB Refining LP, and Excel Paralubes LLC [7][4].
The increase in other income was also significant, primarily from an unrealized gain related to the change in fair value of the investment in NOVONIX [7][4].
Goldman Sachs's revenue rose by 33.2% in fiscal 2021 [1][4].

Additionally, technology expenses and transaction-based expenses were higher, partially offset by significantly lower net provisions for litigation and regulatory proceedings and lower expenses related to consolidated investments (including impairments) [1].
Amgen's revenue rose by 18.6% in fiscal 2024 [1][8].
The revenue growth of 18.6% is directly stated in the database result [8].
The increase in revenue is primarily driven by volume growth of 23%, partially offset by declines in net selling price of 2% [8].
Additionally, product sales from acquired Horizon products contributed significantly, with volume growth of 11% from other brands [3][8].
Caterpillar's revenue rose by 22.1% in fiscal 2021 [5][7].

The increase in revenue was primarily due to higher sales volume, driven by higher end-user demand for equipment and services and the impact from changes in dealer inventories, along with favorable price realization [3][7].
Dealers decreased their inventories about $2.9 billion in 2020, compared to a decrease of about $100 million in 2021 [7].
Realty Income's revenue rose by 60.7% in fiscal 2022 [1][3].
The increase in revenue is primarily due to the merger with VEREIT and acquisitions for the years ended December 31, 2022 and 2021 [8][3].
Specifically, the rental revenue (excluding reimbursable) increased by $1,154,868,000, or 74.1%, from $1,560,171,000 in fiscal 2021 to $3,114,975,000 in fiscal 2022 [8].
The rental revenue (reimbursable) also saw a significant increase, rising by $79,831,000, or 100.4%, from $79,362,000 in fiscal 2021 to $184,682,000 in fiscal 2022 [8].
Oracle's revenue rose by 17.7% in fiscal 2023 [1][8].
The increase in revenue was driven by growth in Oracle's cloud and license business, which contributed 83% of total revenues [1][2].
This growth was attributed to revenue contributions from the acquisition of Cerner and increases in cloud services and license support revenues [1][2].
Additionally, the hardware business saw an increase in revenues, particularly in Oracle Exadata and certain other strategic hardware product offerings [1].
Services revenues also increased, driven by growth in each of Oracle's primary services offerings [1][3].
The overall revenue growth was partially offset by a decrease in cloud license and on-premise license revenues in the cloud and license business [1][2].
Newmont's revenue rose by 58.2% in fiscal 2024 [1][4].

The revenue growth was driven by higher average realized prices for all metals, lower impairment charges, lower reclamation and remediation costs, and higher net income at Peñasquito, partially offset by the loss on assets held for sale and higher income and mining tax expenses [4].
Additionally, the acquisition of Newcrest contributed $1,047 to the increase in net income [4].
These figures in the data show the revenue growth percentage as 58.2% [1][4].
Comcast's revenue rose by 12.4% in fiscal 2021, which ended on December 31, 2021 [3].
Growth in the NBCUniversal segments, driven by increased revenue in the Media, Theme Parks, and Studios segments [1].
Growth in the Cable Communications segment, driven by increased broadband, wireless, business services, advertising, video, and other revenue, partially offset by decreased voice revenue [1][4].
Growth in the Sky segment, driven by increased advertising and direct-to-consumer revenue, partially offset by decreased content revenue, as well as the impact of foreign currency translation [1].
